## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (K8sSecurityBaseline)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8securitybaseline
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sSecurityBaseline
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8securitybaseline
      violation["RunAsNonRoot"] { input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true }
      violation["ReadOnlyRoot"] { input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem != true }
      violation["NoNETAdmin"] { input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.capabilities.NET_ADMIN == true }
```

questions.explanation:
## How It Works

Edge layers cache per-tenant state and call a central Redis-backed ledger via a Lua script that atomically consumes tokens. A regional coordinator ensures global quotas while keeping latency low. Time windows and heartbeat-based refresh bound drift. In Redis outage, fall back to in-process counters with strict backpressure and reconcile on recovery.

## Key Points

- **Atomicity**: Lua script executes in Redis to decrement tokens atomically.
- **Consistency**: cross-region quotas converge via central ledger with short TTL-based caches.
- **Failure handling**: circuit breaker, degraded mode with local counters, paced release when Redis returns.

## Example

```javascript
// Minimal working example
async function checkQuota(tenantId, tokens=1){
  const key = `quota:${tenantId}`;
  const now = Date.now();
  const lua = `
    local k = KEYS[1]
    local t = tonumber(ARGV[1])
    local rate = tonumber(ARGV[2])
    local cap = tonumber(ARGV[3])
    local need = tonumber(ARGV[4])
    local data = redis.call('hmget', k, 'tokens','last')
    local lol = tonumber(data[1] or cap)
    local last = tonumber(data[2] or now)
    local elapsed = math.max(0, now - last)
    lol = math.min(cap, lol + elapsed * rate / 1000)
    if lol >= need then
      lol = lol - need
      redis.call('hmset', k, 'tokens', lol, 'last', now)
      return lol
    else
      return -1
    end
  `
  const res = await redis.eval(lua, 1, key, now, rate, cap, tokens)
  return res
}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question demonstrates end-to-end supply chain security expertise: image signing, SBOM provenance tracking, CVE scanning, and runtime verification in a multi-cloud, high-stakes environment. It tests knowledge of Sigstore ecosystem tools and policy enforcement.

- Image signing with Cosign/Sigstore for supply chain integrity
- CycloneDX SBOM generation for component transparency
- CVE scanning integration (e.g., Trivy, Snyk) for vulnerability detection
- Gatekeeper/OPA policy for runtime enforcement
- Canary deployments and rollback strategies in multi-cloud contexts

## Code Example

### GitHub Actions Workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`)
```yaml
name: Image Provenance Gate
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  build-scan-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate CycloneDX SBOM
        uses: cyclonedx/ghcr-create-sbom@v1
        with:
          format: json
          output-file: sbom.json
      
      - name: Run CVE scan
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        with:
          image-ref: 'ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}'
          format: json
          exit-code: '1'
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
      
      - name: Sign image with Cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
        with:
          cosign-version: 'v2'
      - name: Sign image
        run: |
          cosign sign --yes ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }} -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json
```

### Gatekeeper Policy (`constraint-template.yaml`)
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: requirecosignsignature
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: RequireCosignSignature
      targets:
        - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
          rego: |
            package requirecosignsignature
            violation["image is not signed with Cosign"] {
              image := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].image
              notcosign.verify(image)
            }
```

### Failing Manifest (Unsigned Image)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: unsigned-app
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: ghcr.io/org/app:unsigned-latest
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8080
```

### Passing Manifest (Signed Image)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: signed-app
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8080
```

### Verification Steps
```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0

# Verify SBOM exists
cosign verify-attestation --type cyclonedx ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0

# Verify against Gatekeeper policy
kubectl get requirecosignsignature
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Multi-tenant clusters need strict API access control; SPIFFE identity ensures only trusted services can perform sensitive calls. Gatekeeper + OPA enforces runtime policy with centralized visibility.

## Key Concepts
- OPA Gatekeeper
- ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- SPIFFE IDs and SVIDs
- Kubernetes API verbs and RBAC implications
- Validation via audit logs and Gatekeeper status

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sapicnst
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sApiConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
      rego: |
        package k8sapi
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
          input.review.object.metadata.namespace != "monitoring"
          not allowed_spiffe(input.review.object)
          msg := sprintf("Pod %s in namespace %s cannot use API verb %s", [input.review.object.metadata.name, input.review.object.metadata.namespace, input.review.operation])
        }
        allowed_spiffe(pod) {
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"]
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"] in data.constraint.spec.allowedSVIDs
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sApiConstraint
metadata:
  name: restrict-api-verbs
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
  allowedSVIDs:
    - "spiffe://ibm.com/workload/web"
    - "spiffe://tesla.com/workload/monitor"
    - "spiffe://cloudflare.com/workload/edge"
```

## Validation Plan
1. Deploy ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
2. Test compliant GET request from approved SPIFFE ID
3. Test noncompliant POST request from unapproved SPIFFE ID
4. Verify denial in Gatekeeper audit logs
5. Confirm monitoring namespace bypass works correctly

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (RBACWhitelist)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: rbacwhitelist
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names: {}
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package rbacwhitelist
      violation[{msg}] {
        binding := input.review.object
        binding.kind == \"RoleBinding\" or binding.kind == \"ClusterRoleBinding\"
        role := binding.roleRef.name
        ns := binding.metadata.namespace
        allowed := data.allowlist[ns]
        role != \"\"; role notin allowed
        msg := sprintf(\"RBAC violation: %s bound to %s in %s\", [binding.kind, role, ns])
      }
```

```yaml

apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: RbacWhitelist
metadata:

spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: [\"rbac.authorization.k8s.io\"]
      kinds: [\"RoleBinding\", \"ClusterRoleBinding\"]
  parameters:
    namespaceAllowlists:
      production: [\"view\", \"edit\"]
```
